query: Consider the following context: High entropy alloys have excellent wear resistance, so they have great application prospects in the fields of wear resistance and surface protection. In that context, which material can be used for adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A high entropy alloy (HEA) coating, specifically a CrMnFeCoNi alloy, can be used to adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, enhancing its wear resistance due to the formation of a stable oxide layer and the inherent high hardness of the HEA.
generation.intervention: Deposition of a CrMnFeCoNi high entropy alloy coating
generation.conditions: Coating thickness of 100 micrometers, deposited using magnetron sputtering at a substrate temperature of 200°C
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable oxide layer at the interface between the Cu matrix and the HEA coating
generation.mechanism: The high entropy alloy coating enhances wear resistance by forming a stable oxide layer that prevents metal-to-metal contact and reduces adhesive wear, while its high hardness resists abrasive wear
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% increase in wear resistance compared to the uncoated Cu matrix, measured as a reduction in volume loss per unit distance slid under a load of 10 N
generation.uncertainty: The actual wear resistance enhancement may vary depending on the specific deposition conditions, coating thickness, and testing parameters, and the HEA coating may also introduce residual stresses that affect the Cu matrix

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test using a ball-on-disk tribometer
measurements: Volume loss per unit distance slid
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured wear resistance of the HEA-coated Cu matrix is not at least 20% higher than that of the uncoated Cu matrix, the hypothesis is falsified
